<!--
================================================================================
WHAT THIS DOCUMENT DOES
================================================================================
Question: on an individual chromatin fiber, is accessibility (an overlapping
MSP) at one enhancer summit independent of accessibility at another summit in
the same enhancer?

  codependency = observed co-accessibility - expected under independence
               = P(acc1 & acc2) - P(acc1) * P(acc2)

  > 0  the two summits open together more often than chance (cooperative)
  = 0  independent
  < 0  mutually exclusive / anti-correlated

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DESIGN DECISIONS BAKED IN (all three matter for correctness)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  (1) COMMON FIBER POPULATION. Marginals P(acc1), P(acc2) are computed on
      exactly the same fibers as the joint P(acc1 & acc2), so `observed` and
      `expected` are commensurable. fiber_set = "all_summits" (default)
      restricts once, up front, to fibers spanning every summit of that
      enhancer -- one population for the whole enhancer, so pairs are
      comparable to each other as well. fiber_set = "pair" uses the per-pair
      spanning-both population instead (more fibers per pair, but marginals
      differ between pairs).

  (2) PER REPLICATE, THEN STRATIFIED POOLING. Everything is computed separately
      per Sample. Replicates are combined with a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test
      stratified by replicate, NOT by pooling fibers -- pooling fibers across
      replicates with different marginal accessibility can invert the apparent
      association (Simpson's paradox).

  (3) FISHER TEST ON THE 2x2 TABLE.
                        acc2 = TRUE   acc2 = FALSE
        acc1 = TRUE         n11            n10
        acc1 = FALSE        n01            n00
      `expected = p1 * p2` is derived from this table's own margins, so
      H0: independence IS H0: observed = expected. The Fisher p-value is
      therefore the p-value for "observed differs from expected", and the odds
      ratio is the accompanying effect size. (A test treating `expected` as a
      fixed external constant would be wrong: it is estimated from the same
      fibers and carries its own sampling error.)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
FLOW
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  0   CONFIG -- file paths, enhancers, samples, parameters (edit only this)
  1   BED parser + data loading
  2   Marginal accessibility per summit
  3   Tetrachoric correlation (threshold-invariant sensitivity measure)
      Per-replicate co-dependency (2x2 -> obs / exp / Fisher / bootstrap)
  4   Mantel-Haenszel pooling, Woolf homogeneity, DMSO-vs-dTag (ROR)
  5   Plot functions
  6   RUN -- one pass per enhancer
  7   MAIN FIGURES
        <label>_codep_oddsratio_groups_min<w>.pdf     (forest, pooled OR)
        <label>_codep_triangles_colouronly_min<w>.pdf (LD-style triangles)
  8   COMBINED SUMMARY WORKBOOK (both enhancers, one file)
  9   Optional supplementary figures + MSP-width sweep (off by default)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
OUTPUTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  FIG_DIR    ENH2_codep_oddsratio_groups_min100.pdf
             ENH2_codep_triangles_colouronly_min100.pdf
             ENH3_codep_oddsratio_groups_min100.pdf
             ENH3_codep_triangles_colouronly_min100.pdf
  TABLE_DIR  ENH2_ENH3_codependency_metrics_min100.xlsx
================================================================================
-->

# 0. Config

Everything that should ever need editing lives in this section. File paths
first, then the enhancer definitions, then the analysis parameters.

```{r config-paths}
# =============================================================================
# 0a. FILE PATHS
# =============================================================================

# Root of the fiberHMM results tree. Every sample lives in
#   <MSP_ROOT>/<run_id>/fiberHMM_v2.9.7/<run_id>.recalled_msp.bed
MSP_ROOT       <- ".../min3/results"
FIBERHMM_SUBDIR <- "fiberHMM_v2.9.7"

# Where figures and the metrics workbook are written.
FIG_DIR   <- "..."
TABLE_DIR <- FIG_DIR

dir.create(FIG_DIR,   showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(TABLE_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# run_id -> full path to that sample's recalled MSP BED.
.msp_path <- function(run_id) {
  file.path(MSP_ROOT, run_id, FIBERHMM_SUBDIR, paste0(run_id, ".recalled_msp.bed"))
}

# Sample library. Names on the left are the `Sample` labels used everywhere
# downstream (and parsed for "repN" in figure labels); values are run_ids.
MSP_FILES <- c(
  "SNAI_rep1_DMSO5min"   = .msp_path("SNAI1FVSNAI2KO_rep1_DMSO5min"),
  "SNAI_rep2_DMSO5min"   = .msp_path("SNAI1FVSNAI2KO_rep2_DMSO5min"),
  "SNAI_rep1_dTag5min"   = .msp_path("SNAI1FVSNAI2KO_rep1_dTag5min"),
  "SNAI_rep2_dTag5min"   = .msp_path("SNAI1FVSNAI2KO_rep2_dTag5min"),
  "TWIST1_rep1_DMSO5min" = .msp_path("TWIST1FV_rep1_DMSO5min"),
  "TWIST1_rep2_DMSO5min" = .msp_path("TWIST1FV_rep2_DMSO5min"),
  "TWIST1_rep1_dTag5min" = .msp_path("TWIST1FV_rep1_dTag5min"),
  "TWIST1_rep2_dTag5min" = .msp_path("TWIST1FV_rep2_dTag5min")
)
```

```{r config-samples}
# =============================================================================
# 0b. SAMPLE GROUPS
# =============================================================================

# group label -> Samples. The order of this list is the panel / axis order in
# every figure, for any enhancer that uses the group.
SAMPLE_GROUPS <- list(
  "SNAI1-FNV DMSO" = c("SNAI_rep1_DMSO5min",   "SNAI_rep2_DMSO5min"),
  "SNAI1-FNV dTag" = c("SNAI_rep1_dTag5min",   "SNAI_rep2_dTag5min"),
  "TWIST1-FV DMSO" = c("TWIST1_rep1_DMSO5min", "TWIST1_rep2_DMSO5min"),
  "TWIST1-FV dTag" = c("TWIST1_rep1_dTag5min", "TWIST1_rep2_dTag5min")
)

GROUP_COLOURS <- c("SNAI1-FNV DMSO" = "#a83a1b",
                   "SNAI1-FNV dTag" = "#d6957f",
                   "TWIST1-FV DMSO" = "#1b6ca8",
                   "TWIST1-FV dTag" = "#7fb2d6")

# group -> cell line + treatment. Drives the DMSO-vs-dTag comparison: the two
# groups to be contrasted must share a `line` value.
GROUP_META <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,            ~line,       ~treatment,
  "SNAI1-FNV DMSO",  "SNAI1-FNV", "DMSO",
  "SNAI1-FNV dTag",  "SNAI1-FNV", "dTag",
  "TWIST1-FV DMSO",  "TWIST1-FV", "DMSO",
  "TWIST1-FV dTag",  "TWIST1-FV", "dTag"
)

REF_TREATMENT <- "DMSO"   # denominator of the ratio of odds ratios
```

```{r config-params}
# =============================================================================
# 0d. ANALYSIS PARAMETERS
# =============================================================================

# Minimum MSP width for the main figures. Filters MSPs, never fibers, so the
# analysis population (and therefore n_fibers) is unaffected by it.
MIN_WIDTH <- 100

# Fiber population: "all_summits" (one common population per enhancer, so pairs
# are mutually comparable) or "pair" (per-pair spanning-both population).
FIBER_SET <- "all_summits"

# Replicate x pair combinations below this are flagged `low_fibers`.
MIN_FIBERS <- 20

# Bootstrap draws for the percentile CI on obs-exp (0 = skip).
N_BOOT <- 2000

# Multiple-testing correction. Scope "group" adjusts within each sample group,
# within each enhancer -- the groups are separate experiments and the two
# enhancers are separate analyses, so nothing is adjusted across those.
P_ADJUST_METHOD <- "BH"
P_ADJUST_SCOPE  <- "group"

# Tolerances for the tetrachoric direction check (section 4b). A comparison in
# which neither measure moves appreciably carries no directional information,
# so it is recorded as NA rather than being scored as agreement or as a
# contradiction. RHO_TOL is on the correlation scale; OR_TOL is a fold change
# in the odds ratio.
RHO_TOL <- 0.01
OR_TOL  <- 1.05

# Supplementary outputs: numbered triangles, per-replicate dotplot,
# observed-vs-expected bars, and the MSP-width sensitivity sweep.
# FALSE = only the two main figures + the combined workbook are produced.
MAKE_SUPPLEMENTARY <- FALSE
WIDTH_SWEEP <- c(none = NA, `100` = 100, `150` = 150, `200` = 200, `250` = 250)

# Figure labels contain "≥" and a Unicode minus; cairo renders those correctly.
# Fall back to the base pdf device if this R build has no cairo support.
PDF_DEV <- if (isTRUE(capabilities("cairo"))) grDevices::cairo_pdf else grDevices::pdf

# Bootstrap reproducibility. The seed is re-set at the START of each enhancer
# (see run_enhancer), not once for the whole document -- otherwise the second
# enhancer would inherit whatever RNG state the first one left behind, and its
# bootstrap CIs would change if you added, removed or reordered enhancers.
BOOT_SEED <- 1
```

```{r deps, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# 0e. DEPENDENCIES
# =============================================================================
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)       # read_fiberhmm_bed() uses read_lines() / read_tsv()
library(tibble)

# base R only gained %||% in 4.4; define it unconditionally so the code runs on
# older installs too.
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a

# fiberHMM BED lines are long (many blocks per read); readr's default
# connection buffer truncates them, which shows up as bogus field counts.
Sys.setenv("VROOM_CONNECTION_SIZE" = 500072)
```

```{r config-check}
# Fail immediately on a malformed config rather than three chunks later.
stopifnot(
  length(ENHANCERS) >= 1,
  !is.null(names(ENHANCERS)), !anyDuplicated(names(ENHANCERS)),
  !anyDuplicated(names(MSP_FILES)),
  setequal(GROUP_META$group, names(SAMPLE_GROUPS)),
  all(names(SAMPLE_GROUPS) %in% names(GROUP_COLOURS)),
  all(unlist(SAMPLE_GROUPS, use.names = FALSE) %in% names(MSP_FILES)),
  REF_TREATMENT %in% GROUP_META$treatment
)

for (lab in names(ENHANCERS)) {
  e <- ENHANCERS[[lab]]
  stopifnot(
    length(e$summits) >= 2,                       # need >= 1 pair
    !is.null(names(e$summits)), !any(is.na(e$summits)),
    !anyDuplicated(names(e$summits)),
    length(e$chrom) == 1,
    all(e$groups %in% names(SAMPLE_GROUPS))
  )
}

# Only the samples some enhancer actually needs are loaded.
SAMPLES_USED <- unique(unlist(SAMPLE_GROUPS[unique(unlist(
  lapply(ENHANCERS, `[[`, "groups")))], use.names = FALSE))
message("Enhancers: ", paste(names(ENHANCERS), collapse = ", "),
        " | samples to load: ", length(SAMPLES_USED))
```

# 1. BED parser and data loading

```{r parser-fn}
# 13 standard columns written by fiberHMM v2.9.7 footprint BEDs (no TF score
# columns). 15-column TF files use the extended set built inline below.
BED_COLS_13 <- c("chrom", "chromStart", "chromEnd", "name", "score", "strand",
                 "thickStart", "thickEnd", "itemRgb", "blockCount",
                 "blockSizes", "chromStarts", "blockRgb")

BED_COLS_15 <- c("chrom", "chromStart", "chromEnd", "name", "score", "strand",
                 "thickStart", "thickEnd", "itemRgb", "blockCount",
                 "blockSizes", "chromStarts", "blockTq", "blockEl", "blockEr")

# NOTE ON COORDINATES -- read this before setting SUMMITS.
# This parser converts everything out of BED's 0-based half-open space and into
# 1-based inclusive coordinates:
#   reads      read_start = chromStart + 1L
#              read_end   = chromEnd
#   footprints fp_start   = chromStart + chromStarts + 1L
#              fp_end     = chromStart + chromStarts + blockSizes
# Both tables are therefore 1-based inclusive, and the overlap test used
# throughout this document -- `start <= pos & end >= pos` -- is exactly right,
# with no off-by-one. The consequence: SUMMITS must be given in 1-based
# coordinates. If you are pulling summits out of a MACS narrowPeak, add 1.
read_fiberhmm_bed <- function(path) {
  lines    <- readr::read_lines(path)
  n_fields <- stringr::str_count(lines, "\t") + 1

  # auto-detect format: 13 cols = v2.9.7 footprint, 15 cols = older tf format
  expected <- as.integer(names(which.max(table(n_fields))))
  if (!expected %in% c(13L, 15L)) {
    warning(sprintf("%s: unexpected field count %d", path, expected))
  }
  cols_to_use <- if (expected == 15L) BED_COLS_15 else BED_COLS_13

  # Malformed rows (the blockEl/blockEr fusion writer bug) are dropped, which
  # is why anything downstream must join on read_name and never positionally.
  bad <- which(n_fields != expected)
  if (length(bad) > 0) {
    warning(sprintf("%s: %d malformed row(s) dropped (line numbers: %s)",
                    path, length(bad), paste(utils::head(bad, 10), collapse = ", ")))
    lines <- lines[-bad]
  }

  raw <- readr::read_tsv(
    I(paste(lines, collapse = "\n")),
    col_names = cols_to_use,
    col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character(),
                            chromStart = "i", chromEnd = "i",
                            score      = "i", thickStart = "i",
                            thickEnd   = "i", blockCount = "i")
  )

  reads_tbl <- raw %>%
    dplyr::transmute(read_name  = name,
                     read_start = chromStart + 1L,
                     read_end   = chromEnd,
                     read_score = score,
                     strand)

  # Only the columns that exist are unnested. blockTq is present on 15-column
  # TF files only; unnesting a NULL column alongside two size-k columns is the
  # case where tidyr's behaviour has changed between versions (some error, some
  # silently drop the row), which would empty $footprints and turn every
  # co-dependency number into 0 / NA. check_parser() below verifies the count.
  unnest_cols <- c("blockSizes", "chromStarts")
  fps_tbl <- raw %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      read_name   = name,
      read_start  = chromStart,
      blockSizes  = lapply(strsplit(blockSizes,  ","), as.integer),
      chromStarts = lapply(strsplit(chromStarts, ","), as.integer)
    ) %>%
    tidyr::unnest(dplyr::all_of(unnest_cols)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      fp_start = read_start + chromStarts + 1L,
      fp_end   = read_start + chromStarts + blockSizes,
      fp_width = blockSizes
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(read_name, fp_start, fp_end, fp_width)

  list(reads = reads_tbl, footprints = fps_tbl)
}

# Parser sanity check: run on ONE file before the whole analysis runs on eight.
# n_footprints must equal sum(blockCount) to within rounding.
check_parser <- function(path) {
  obj   <- read_fiberhmm_bed(path)
  lines <- readr::read_lines(path, progress = FALSE)
  lines <- lines[!grepl("^(#|track|browser|$)", lines)]
  f     <- stringr::str_split_fixed(lines, "\t", 11)
  expected_blocks <- sum(as.integer(f[, 10]), na.rm = TRUE)   # blockCount col
  tibble::tibble(
    file             = basename(path),
    n_data_lines     = length(lines),
    n_reads_returned = nrow(obj$reads),
    n_reads_dropped  = length(lines) - nrow(obj$reads),
    n_footprints     = nrow(obj$footprints),
    expected_blocks  = expected_blocks,
    blocks_ok        = nrow(obj$footprints) > 0 &&
                       abs(nrow(obj$footprints) - expected_blocks) <=
                         expected_blocks * 0.01,
    coords_1based    = min(obj$footprints$fp_start) > 0
  )
}
```

```{r load-fn}
# read_fiberhmm_bed() returns chrom in neither $reads nor $footprints, so chrom
# is recovered from column 1 of the BED and matched on read_name (column 4).
# It must be matched on read_name, NOT positionally: malformed rows are dropped
# before the parser returns, so nrow(obj$reads) can be smaller than the number
# of data lines and any positional scheme silently shifts every chrom after the
# first dropped line. The map is de-duplicated first, so a repeated read_name
# cannot multiply fibers (which a plain left_join would do).
.bed_chrom_map <- function(path) {
  lines <- readr::read_lines(path, progress = FALSE)
  lines <- lines[!grepl("^(#|track|browser|$)", lines)]
  f <- stringr::str_split_fixed(lines, "\t", 5)   # cols 1..4 + remainder
  tibble::tibble(read_name = f[, 4], chrom = f[, 1]) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(read_name, .keep_all = TRUE)
}

# Read and pool every MSP .bed file into:
#   $reads : one row per fiber (chrom, Sample, unique_id, read_start, read_end)
#            -- the full aligned span, needed to know whether a fiber even
#            reaches a summit (fibers that don't span it cannot be scored)
#   $msps  : one row per accessible patch (chrom, Sample, unique_id,
#            start, end, width)
# unique_id = Sample + read_name, so identical read names across samples stay
# distinct once the tables are bound together.
load_msp_data <- function(msp_files) {
  missing <- msp_files[!file.exists(msp_files)]
  if (length(missing) > 0) {
    stop("MSP file(s) not found:\n", paste(missing, collapse = "\n"))
  }
  if (is.null(names(msp_files)) || any(names(msp_files) == "")) {
    stop("msp_files must be a NAMED vector; names become the Sample column.")
  }

  loaded <- purrr::imap(msp_files, function(path, s_name) {
    obj       <- read_fiberhmm_bed(path)
    chrom_map <- .bed_chrom_map(path)

    reads <- obj$reads %>%
      dplyr::left_join(chrom_map, by = "read_name") %>%
      dplyr::transmute(chrom, Sample = s_name,
                       unique_id = paste0(s_name, "_", read_name),
                       read_start, read_end)

    msps <- obj$footprints %>%
      dplyr::left_join(chrom_map, by = "read_name") %>%
      dplyr::transmute(chrom, Sample = s_name,
                       unique_id = paste0(s_name, "_", read_name),
                       start = fp_start, end = fp_end, width = fp_width)

    if (anyNA(reads$chrom) || anyNA(msps$chrom)) {
      warning(sprintf("%s: %d reads / %d MSPs got no chrom from the BED.",
                      s_name, sum(is.na(reads$chrom)), sum(is.na(msps$chrom))))
    }
    if (nrow(msps) == 0) {
      stop(sprintf("%s: read_fiberhmm_bed() returned 0 footprints -- run check_parser().",
                   s_name))
    }
    list(reads = reads, msps = msps)
  })

  out <- list(reads = dplyr::bind_rows(purrr::map(loaded, "reads")),
              msps  = dplyr::bind_rows(purrr::map(loaded, "msps")))
  message(sprintf("Loaded %d samples: %d fibers, %d MSPs.",
                  length(msp_files), nrow(out$reads), nrow(out$msps)))
  out
}

# Shared coordinate / width / sample filtering. The argument is `chrom_sel`,
# not `chrom`, so it can never be shadowed by the `chrom` COLUMN inside filter().
.prep_inputs <- function(reads, msps, chrom_sel = NULL, min_width = NULL,
                         samples = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(chrom_sel)) {
    if (!"chrom" %in% names(reads)) stop("`reads` has no chrom column.")
    reads <- reads %>% dplyr::filter(chrom %in% chrom_sel)
    msps  <- msps  %>% dplyr::filter(chrom %in% chrom_sel)
  }
  if (!is.null(min_width) && !is.na(min_width)) {
    msps <- msps %>% dplyr::filter(width >= min_width)
  }
  if (!is.null(samples)) {
    reads <- reads %>% dplyr::filter(Sample %in% samples)
    msps  <- msps  %>% dplyr::filter(Sample %in% samples)
  }
  list(reads = reads, msps = msps)
}
```

```{r load-data}
# Parser check on one file first -- fails fast and cheaply if the import is wrong.
check_parser(MSP_FILES[[SAMPLES_USED[1]]])

# Loaded ONCE for all enhancers; each enhancer then filters by chrom + samples.
d <- load_msp_data(MSP_FILES[SAMPLES_USED])
```

# 2. Marginal accessibility per summit

```{r accessibility-fns}
# Per fiber: is there an MSP overlapping `pos`? Restricted to fibers that
# structurally span `pos` (a fiber that does not reach the summit is not
# evidence of inaccessibility).
.accessibility_at <- function(reads, msps, pos) {
  spanning <- reads %>% dplyr::filter(read_start <= pos, read_end >= pos)
  hit_ids  <- msps %>% dplyr::filter(start <= pos, end >= pos) %>%
    dplyr::pull(unique_id) %>% unique()
  spanning %>% dplyr::mutate(accessible = unique_id %in% hit_ids)
}

# Marginal accessibility for each named summit position.
#
# CAUTION when reading the output: this uses every fiber spanning THAT summit,
# which is a larger population than the all-summits set used for the
# co-dependency tables. So `fraction_accessible` here and `frac_peak1` /
# `frac_peak2` in the per-replicate table are not the same quantity and should
# not be compared directly.
compute_summit_accessibility <- function(reads, msps, summits,
                                         chrom_sel = NULL, min_width = NULL,
                                         samples = NULL, by_sample = FALSE) {
  p <- .prep_inputs(reads, msps, chrom_sel, min_width, samples)
  reads <- p$reads; msps <- p$msps

  one <- function(reads, msps, tag = NA_character_) {
    purrr::imap_dfr(summits, function(pos, label) {
      acc <- .accessibility_at(reads, msps, pos)
      if (nrow(acc) == 0) {
        warning(sprintf("Summit '%s' at %s:%d: NO reads span this position.",
                        label, chrom_sel %||% "?", pos))
        return(tibble::tibble(Sample = tag, summit = label, position = pos,
                              n_reads_spanning    = 0L,
                              n_accessible        = 0L,
                              fraction_accessible = NA_real_))
      }
      tibble::tibble(Sample = tag, summit = label, position = pos,
                     n_reads_spanning    = nrow(acc),
                     n_accessible        = sum(acc$accessible),
                     fraction_accessible = mean(acc$accessible))
    })
  }

  if (!by_sample) return(one(reads, msps) %>% dplyr::select(-Sample))

  purrr::map_dfr(sort(unique(reads$Sample)), function(s) {
    one(reads %>% dplyr::filter(Sample == s),
        msps  %>% dplyr::filter(Sample == s), tag = s)
  })
}
```

# 3. Per-replicate co-dependency

```{r tetrachoric-fn}
# =============================================================================
# TETRACHORIC CORRELATION -- sensitivity analysis for the odds ratio
# =============================================================================
# The odds ratio is the effect size reported throughout, but it is not
# invariant to the marginals under a threshold model. If per-fiber
# accessibility is a binary readout of an underlying continuous propensity to
# open, then a treatment that shifts the marginal accessibility also moves the
# threshold, and the odds ratio changes even when the underlying association is
# unchanged. Because the treatments here DO shift marginal accessibility
# substantially, the DMSO-vs-dTag comparison needs a check that the change in
# association is not an artifact of that shift.
#
# The tetrachoric correlation is that check: it is the correlation of the
# latent bivariate normal that would produce the observed 2x2 table given its
# own margins, so it is invariant to the thresholds by construction. If the
# tetrachoric correlation moves in the same direction as the odds ratio, the
# marginal shift is not driving the result.
#
# IMPLEMENTATION. No extra package is needed. For a standard bivariate normal
# with correlation r,
#     d/dr P(X > h, Y > k; r) = phi2(h, k; r),
# the bivariate normal density, so
#     P(X > h, Y > k; r) = P(X > h) P(Y > k) + integral_0^r phi2(h, k; t) dt,
# a one-dimensional integral that stats::integrate() evaluates to machine
# precision. The tetrachoric correlation is then the r solving
#     P(X > h, Y > k; r) = n11 / n,  with  h = qnorm(1 - p1), k = qnorm(1 - p2).
# This was verified against mvtnorm/scipy bivariate normal CDFs to ~1e-16.

.bvn_upper <- function(h, k, r) {
  base <- stats::pnorm(-h) * stats::pnorm(-k)
  if (r == 0) return(base)
  dens <- function(t) {
    (1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(1 - t^2))) *
      exp(-(h^2 - 2 * t * h * k + k^2) / (2 * (1 - t^2)))
  }
  base + stats::integrate(dens, 0, r, rel.tol = 1e-10)$value
}

# Tetrachoric correlation of a 2x2 table. Returns NA only when the latent
# correlation is genuinely not identified (a degenerate margin) or when the
# integral fails -- and the latter warns rather than failing silently.
#
# P(X > h, Y > k; r) increases monotonically in r, so f() below is increasing.
# If the root lies outside +/-0.999 the association is stronger than the search
# interval can express; that is the strong-coupling case this analysis most
# cares about, so the value is CLAMPED to the boundary and flagged rather than
# discarded as NA (uniroot would otherwise just error with "values at end
# points not of opposite sign").
tetrachoric_rho <- function(n11, n10, n01, n00, warn = TRUE) {
  n <- n11 + n10 + n01 + n00
  if (n == 0) return(NA_real_)
  p1 <- (n11 + n10) / n
  p2 <- (n11 + n01) / n
  if (p1 <= 0 || p1 >= 1 || p2 <= 0 || p2 >= 1) return(NA_real_)
  h <- stats::qnorm(1 - p1)
  k <- stats::qnorm(1 - p2)
  target <- n11 / n
  f <- function(r) .bvn_upper(h, k, r) - target
  lim <- 0.999

  ends <- tryCatch(c(f(-lim), f(lim)),
                   error = function(e) {
                     if (warn) warning("tetrachoric_rho: bivariate normal ",
                                       "integral failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
                     c(NA_real_, NA_real_)
                   })
  if (anyNA(ends)) return(NA_real_)
  if (ends[1] > 0) return(-lim)   # root below -0.999: clamp
  if (ends[2] < 0) return( lim)   # root above +0.999: clamp

  tryCatch(stats::uniroot(f, interval = c(-lim, lim), tol = 1e-10)$root,
           error = function(e) {
             if (warn) warning("tetrachoric_rho: uniroot failed: ",
                               conditionMessage(e))
             NA_real_
           })
}
```

```{r codep-helpers}
# Fibers spanning EVERY summit. Reads are contiguous intervals and summits are
# single positions, so spanning the two extreme summits implies spanning all.
.fibers_spanning_all <- function(reads, summits) {
  pos <- unlist(summits, use.names = FALSE)
  reads %>% dplyr::filter(read_start <= min(pos), read_end >= max(pos))
}

.fibers_spanning_pair <- function(reads, pos1, pos2) {
  reads %>% dplyr::filter(read_start <= min(pos1, pos2),
                          read_end   >= max(pos1, pos2))
}

# Tag each fiber accessible / not at every summit (>= 1 overlapping MSP).
.acc_flags <- function(fibers, msps, summits) {
  out <- fibers %>% dplyr::select(Sample, unique_id)
  for (lab in names(summits)) {
    pos <- summits[[lab]]
    hit <- msps %>%
      dplyr::filter(start <= pos, end >= pos) %>%
      dplyr::pull(unique_id) %>% unique()
    out[[paste0("acc_", lab)]] <- out$unique_id %in% hit
  }
  out
}

# One replicate, one summit pair: 2x2 table -> obs / exp / codependency + Fisher.
.codep_one <- function(a1, a2, boot = 0) {
  n11 <- sum(a1 & a2);  n10 <- sum(a1 & !a2)
  n01 <- sum(!a1 & a2); n00 <- sum(!a1 & !a2)
  n   <- n11 + n10 + n01 + n00
  if (n == 0) return(NULL)

  p1  <- (n11 + n10) / n          # marginal at summit 1, THIS fiber set
  p2  <- (n11 + n01) / n          # marginal at summit 2, THIS fiber set
  obs <- n11 / n
  exp <- p1 * p2

  tbl <- matrix(c(n11, n10, n01, n00), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
  ft  <- suppressWarnings(stats::fisher.test(tbl))

  res <- tibble::tibble(
    n_fibers = n, n11 = n11, n10 = n10, n01 = n01, n00 = n00,
    frac_peak1 = p1, frac_peak2 = p2,
    observed_coaccessibility = obs,
    expected_coaccessibility = exp,
    codependency = obs - exp,
    odds_ratio = unname(ft$estimate),
    or_ci_lo   = ft$conf.int[1],
    or_ci_hi   = ft$conf.int[2],
    p_fisher   = ft$p.value,
    # Threshold-invariant companion to the odds ratio (see tetrachoric-fn).
    rho_tetrachoric = tetrachoric_rho(n11, n10, n01, n00)
  )

  # Percentile bootstrap on codependency. Fibers are resampled and BOTH the
  # marginals and the joint are recomputed on each resample, as they must be.
  if (boot > 0) {
    bv <- purrr::map_dbl(seq_len(boot), function(i) {
      idx <- sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE)
      b1 <- a1[idx]; b2 <- a2[idx]
      mean(b1 & b2) - mean(b1) * mean(b2)
    })
    res$boot_ci_lo <- unname(stats::quantile(bv, 0.025))
    res$boot_ci_hi <- unname(stats::quantile(bv, 0.975))
  } else {
    res$boot_ci_lo <- NA_real_
    res$boot_ci_hi <- NA_real_
  }
  res
}
```

```{r codep-main}
# reads, msps   : from load_msp_data()
# summits       : named numeric vector of single-bp positions (1-based)
# sample_groups : named list, group label -> Samples. Used for labelling and
#                 for the p-adjustment scope; NULL = every Sample its own group.
# p_adjust_scope: "group" adjusts within each sample group (recommended -- the
#                 groups are separate experiments); "all" adjusts across the
#                 whole table; "none" leaves p_fisher unadjusted.
compute_codependency_perrep <- function(reads, msps, summits,
                                        chrom_sel = NULL, min_width = NULL,
                                        fiber_set = c("all_summits", "pair"),
                                        samples = NULL,
                                        sample_groups = NULL,
                                        min_fibers = 20,
                                        boot = 0,
                                        p_adjust_method = "BH",
                                        p_adjust_scope = c("group", "all", "none")) {
  fiber_set      <- match.arg(fiber_set)
  p_adjust_scope <- match.arg(p_adjust_scope)
  if (length(summits) < 2) stop("Need at least 2 summits to form a pair.")

  p <- .prep_inputs(reads, msps, chrom_sel, min_width, samples)
  reads <- p$reads; msps <- p$msps
  if (nrow(reads) == 0) stop("compute_codependency_perrep: no fibers left after filtering.")

  grp_of <- function(s) {
    if (is.null(sample_groups)) return(s)
    hit <- names(sample_groups)[vapply(sample_groups, function(v) s %in% v, logical(1))]
    if (length(hit) == 0) NA_character_ else hit[1]
  }

  reps  <- sort(unique(reads$Sample))
  pairs <- utils::combn(names(summits), 2, simplify = FALSE)

  out <- purrr::map_dfr(reps, function(s) {
    r_s <- reads %>% dplyr::filter(Sample == s)
    m_s <- msps  %>% dplyr::filter(Sample == s)

    if (fiber_set == "all_summits") {
      fib <- .fibers_spanning_all(r_s, summits)
      if (nrow(fib) == 0) {
        warning(sprintf("%s: no fibers span all summits -- replicate dropped.", s))
        return(NULL)
      }
      flags <- .acc_flags(fib, m_s, summits)
      purrr::map_dfr(pairs, function(pr) {
        r <- .codep_one(flags[[paste0("acc_", pr[1])]],
                        flags[[paste0("acc_", pr[2])]], boot = boot)
        if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
        dplyr::bind_cols(tibble::tibble(Sample = s, group = grp_of(s),
                                        peak1 = pr[1], peak2 = pr[2]), r)
      })
    } else {
      purrr::map_dfr(pairs, function(pr) {
        pos1 <- summits[[pr[1]]]; pos2 <- summits[[pr[2]]]
        fib  <- .fibers_spanning_pair(r_s, pos1, pos2)
        if (nrow(fib) == 0) {
          warning(sprintf("%s: no fibers span both %s and %s -- pair skipped.",
                          s, pr[1], pr[2]))
          return(NULL)
        }
        flags <- .acc_flags(fib, m_s, summits[pr])
        r <- .codep_one(flags[[paste0("acc_", pr[1])]],
                        flags[[paste0("acc_", pr[2])]], boot = boot)
        if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
        dplyr::bind_cols(tibble::tibble(Sample = s, group = grp_of(s),
                                        peak1 = pr[1], peak2 = pr[2]), r)
      })
    }
  })

  if (nrow(out) == 0) stop("compute_codependency_perrep: nothing computed.")

  out <- out %>%
    dplyr::mutate(pair       = paste(peak1, peak2, sep = " – "),
                  fiber_set  = fiber_set,
                  low_fibers = n_fibers < min_fibers)

  out <- switch(
    p_adjust_scope,
    none  = out %>% dplyr::mutate(p_adj = p_fisher),
    all   = out %>% dplyr::mutate(p_adj = stats::p.adjust(p_fisher, p_adjust_method)),
    group = out %>% dplyr::group_by(group) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(p_adj = stats::p.adjust(p_fisher, p_adjust_method)) %>%
      dplyr::ungroup()
  ) %>%
    dplyr::relocate(pair, .after = peak2)

  if (any(out$low_fibers)) {
    message("Replicate x pair combinations with < ", min_fibers,
            " fibers (flagged `low_fibers`, interpret with caution):\n  ",
            paste(sprintf("%s / %s (n=%d)",
                          out$Sample[out$low_fibers], out$pair[out$low_fibers],
                          out$n_fibers[out$low_fibers]), collapse = "\n  "))
  }
  out
}
```

# 4. Replicate summary, stratified pooling, DMSO vs dTag

```{r summarise-fn}
# mean / sd of codependency across replicates, plus sign consistency.
summarise_codependency_reps <- function(perrep_df, by_group = TRUE) {
  keys <- if (by_group && !all(is.na(perrep_df$group))) c("group", "pair") else "pair"
  perrep_df %>%
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(keys))) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      n_reps       = dplyr::n(),
      mean_codep   = mean(codependency),
      sd_codep     = stats::sd(codependency),
      min_codep    = min(codependency),
      max_codep    = max(codependency),
      same_sign    = length(unique(sign(codependency))) == 1,
      mean_obs     = mean(observed_coaccessibility),
      mean_exp     = mean(expected_coaccessibility),
      # Tetrachoric correlation, averaged over replicates. Averaging the
      # per-replicate values keeps this consistent with the rest of the
      # document: fibers are never pooled across replicates (see design
      # decision 2), so this cannot be inverted by Simpson's paradox the way a
      # rho computed on the replicate-summed table could be.
      # Guarded: mean(na.rm) of an all-NA vector is NaN and min/max are
      # -Inf/Inf, all of which would be written to the sheet as if they were
      # values.
      mean_rho     = if (all(is.na(rho_tetrachoric))) NA_real_ else
                       mean(rho_tetrachoric, na.rm = TRUE),
      min_rho      = if (all(is.na(rho_tetrachoric))) NA_real_ else
                       min(rho_tetrachoric, na.rm = TRUE),
      max_rho      = if (all(is.na(rho_tetrachoric))) NA_real_ else
                       max(rho_tetrachoric, na.rm = TRUE),
      total_fibers = sum(n_fibers),
      any_low_n    = any(low_fibers),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
```

```{r pool-fn}
# Pools the per-replicate 2x2 tables WITHOUT pooling fibers. Returns a common
# odds ratio + CI, an MH p-value, and a Woolf homogeneity check (tests whether
# the OR differs between replicates -- i.e. whether pooling is defensible).
# With only 2 replicates the Woolf test has 1 df and very little power: treat a
# non-significant woolf_p as "no evidence against pooling", not "homogeneous".
#
# WHY THE CI IS COMPUTED HERE INSTEAD OF TAKEN FROM mantelhaen.test():
# mantelhaen.test(exact = FALSE) does return conf.int, but it returns
# c(NaN, NaN) whenever the Robins-Breslow-Greenland variance degenerates --
# which happens as soon as a 2x2 cell is empty in every replicate (then either
# sum(a*d/n) or sum(b*c/n) is 0, the common OR is 0 or Inf, and the variance of
# its log is undefined). That is the usual reason mh_ci_lo/mh_ci_hi come back
# all-NA and no error bars appear in the forest plot.
#
# So: OR, SE(log OR) and CI are computed explicitly by the RBG formula, the
# degenerate case is DETECTED and reported (`any_zero_cell`, `min_cell`), and a
# Haldane-Anscombe fallback (+0.5 to every cell) supplies a finite, clearly
# flagged interval so the figure is not silently empty. `ci_method` records
# which one each row used. se_log_or is what the Wald cross-check below needs.
.mh_or_ci <- function(arr, conf_level = 0.95, haldane_if_degenerate = TRUE) {
  core <- function(a, b, c, d) {
    n  <- a + b + c + d
    R  <- sum(a * d / n);  S <- sum(b * c / n)
    P  <- (a + d) / n;     Q <- (b + c) / n
    or <- R / S
    v  <- sum(P * a * d / n) / (2 * R^2) +
          sum(P * b * c / n + Q * a * d / n) / (2 * R * S) +
          sum(Q * b * c / n) / (2 * S^2)
    list(or = or, se = sqrt(v))
  }
  a <- arr[1, 1, ]; b <- arr[1, 2, ]; c <- arr[2, 1, ]; d <- arr[2, 2, ]
  min_cell   <- min(c(a, b, c, d))
  degenerate <- sum(a * d / (a + b + c + d)) == 0 ||
                sum(b * c / (a + b + c + d)) == 0
  est    <- core(a, b, c, d)
  method <- "Robins-Breslow-Greenland"

  if ((degenerate || !is.finite(est$se)) && haldane_if_degenerate) {
    est    <- core(a + 0.5, b + 0.5, c + 0.5, d + 0.5)
    method <- "RBG after Haldane-Anscombe +0.5 (empty cell)"
  }
  z <- stats::qnorm((1 + conf_level) / 2)
  list(or = est$or,
       se_log_or = est$se,
       ci_lo = est$or * exp(-z * est$se),
       ci_hi = est$or * exp( z * est$se),
       min_cell = min_cell,
       any_zero_cell = min_cell == 0,
       ci_method = method)
}

pool_codependency_mh <- function(perrep_df, by_group = TRUE, exact = FALSE,
                                 p_adjust_method = "BH", conf_level = 0.95) {
  keys <- if (by_group && !all(is.na(perrep_df$group))) c("group", "pair") else "pair"

  woolf <- function(x) {   # Woolf test for homogeneity of odds ratios
    x   <- x + 1 / 2
    k   <- dim(x)[3]
    or  <- apply(x, 3, function(m) (m[1, 1] * m[2, 2]) / (m[1, 2] * m[2, 1]))
    w   <- apply(x, 3, function(m) 1 / sum(1 / m))
    chi <- sum(w * (log(or) - stats::weighted.mean(log(or), w))^2)
    stats::pchisq(chi, k - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
  }

  perrep_df %>%
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(keys))) %>%
    dplyr::group_modify(function(dd, k) {
      arr <- array(NA_integer_, dim = c(2, 2, nrow(dd)))
      for (i in seq_len(nrow(dd))) {
        arr[, , i] <- matrix(c(dd$n11[i], dd$n10[i], dd$n01[i], dd$n00[i]),
                             nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
      }
      ci <- .mh_or_ci(arr, conf_level = conf_level)

      # p-value: CMH for >= 2 strata, Fisher for 1. Guarded, since the CMH
      # variance is also undefined for fully degenerate tables.
      pv <- if (nrow(dd) < 2) {
        tryCatch(suppressWarnings(stats::fisher.test(arr[, , 1])$p.value),
                 error = function(e) NA_real_)
      } else {
        tryCatch(suppressWarnings(stats::mantelhaen.test(arr, exact = exact)$p.value),
                 error = function(e) NA_real_)
      }

      tibble::tibble(
        n_reps        = nrow(dd),
        total_fibers  = sum(arr),
        mh_or         = ci$or,
        mh_ci_lo      = ci$ci_lo,
        mh_ci_hi      = ci$ci_hi,
        se_log_or     = ci$se_log_or,
        p_mh          = pv,
        woolf_p       = tryCatch(woolf(arr), error = function(e) NA_real_),
        min_cell      = ci$min_cell,
        any_zero_cell = ci$any_zero_cell,
        ci_method     = ci$ci_method,
        mh_note       = if (nrow(dd) < 2) "single replicate: Fisher p, not CMH"
                        else if (isTRUE(exact)) "exact CMH p" else "asymptotic CMH p"
      )
    }) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(p_mh_adj = stats::p.adjust(p_mh, method = p_adjust_method))
}
```

```{r or-compare-fn}
# =============================================================================
# Within each cell line, is the summit-summit association DIFFERENT between
# DMSO and dTag? That is a question about a RATIO OF ODDS RATIOS (ROR), i.e. an
# interaction -- NOT something you can answer by noting that one OR is
# significant and the other is not. Two CIs overlapping (or not) is also not a
# test of their difference.
#
#   ROR = OR_dTag / OR_DMSO
#   ROR = 1  association unchanged by dTag
#   ROR < 1  association weaker after dTag (co-dependency lost with the TF)
#   ROR > 1  association stronger after dTag
#
# Two independent routes are computed, and they should broadly agree:
#
#  (1) PRIMARY -- fiber-level logistic regression interaction.
#        acc_b ~ acc_a + Sample + acc_a:treatment
#      `Sample` gives every replicate its own intercept, so replicate-to-
#      replicate differences in baseline accessibility cannot masquerade as a
#      treatment effect. The acc_a:treatment coefficient IS log(ROR), and the
#      likelihood-ratio test of dropping it is the test of "the two odds ratios
#      are equal". log-OR is symmetric, so regressing acc_b on acc_a or acc_a
#      on acc_b gives the identical interaction -- no arbitrary choice of
#      response here.
#
#  (2) CROSS-CHECK -- Wald test on the two pooled MH log odds ratios:
#        z = (log OR_dTag - log OR_DMSO) / sqrt(SE_dTag^2 + SE_DMSO^2)
#      Cruder (it ignores within-replicate structure beyond the MH
#      stratification) but a useful sanity check: if (1) and (2) disagree
#      badly, look at the per-replicate tables before believing either.
# =============================================================================

# Per-fiber accessibility flags for every sample, on the analysis population.
build_fiber_flags <- function(reads, msps, summits, chrom_sel = NULL,
                              min_width = NULL, samples = NULL,
                              fiber_set = c("all_summits", "pair"),
                              pair = NULL) {
  fiber_set <- match.arg(fiber_set)
  p <- .prep_inputs(reads, msps, chrom_sel, min_width, samples)
  purrr::map_dfr(sort(unique(p$reads$Sample)), function(s) {
    r_s <- p$reads %>% dplyr::filter(Sample == s)
    m_s <- p$msps  %>% dplyr::filter(Sample == s)
    sm  <- if (fiber_set == "pair" && !is.null(pair)) summits[pair] else summits
    fib <- if (fiber_set == "all_summits") .fibers_spanning_all(r_s, sm)
           else .fibers_spanning_pair(r_s, sm[[1]], sm[[2]])
    if (nrow(fib) == 0) return(NULL)
    .acc_flags(fib, m_s, sm)
  })
}

# (1) PRIMARY: interaction test, per cell line x summit pair.
# sample_meta: tibble(Sample, group, line, treatment)
compare_or_treatments_glm <- function(reads, msps, summits, sample_meta,
                                      chrom_sel = NULL, min_width = NULL,
                                      fiber_set = "all_summits",
                                      ref_treatment = "DMSO",
                                      p_adjust_method = "BH") {

  if (!ref_treatment %in% sample_meta$treatment) {
    stop(sprintf("ref_treatment '%s' not found in sample_meta$treatment (%s)",
                 ref_treatment, paste(unique(sample_meta$treatment), collapse = ", ")))
  }

  flags <- build_fiber_flags(reads, msps, summits, chrom_sel, min_width,
                             samples = sample_meta$Sample, fiber_set = fiber_set) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(sample_meta, by = "Sample")

  pairs         <- utils::combn(names(summits), 2, simplify = FALSE)
  lines         <- unique(sample_meta$line)
  alt_treatment <- setdiff(unique(sample_meta$treatment), ref_treatment)[1]

  out <- purrr::map_dfr(lines, function(L) {
    purrr::map_dfr(pairs, function(pr) {

      # WHY THE INTERACTION IS AN EXPLICIT NUMERIC COLUMN AND NOT `acc_a:dtag`.
      # R gives a factor FULL indicator coding inside a term whenever the term
      # with that factor deleted is absent from the model. Deleting acc_a from
      # `acc_a:dtag` leaves `dtag`, which has no main effect here (it cannot
      # have one -- it is collinear with Sample, since replicates are nested in
      # treatment). So acc_a is fully dummy-coded and the matrix gets BOTH
      # acc_aFALSE:dtag and acc_aTRUE:dtag; their sum is dtag, which the Sample
      # dummies already span. Rank deficient by one, acc_aTRUE:dtag is pivoted
      # out to NA, and the surviving acc_aFALSE:dtag coefficient is -log(ROR).
      # summary()$coefficients drops aliased rows, so a regex for the term
      # finds exactly one match and every estimability check passes --
      # returning the RECIPROCAL of the intended ratio, with a plausible CI and
      # p-value. The same happens with `acc_a:treatment`, for the same reason.
      #
      # acc_a is therefore coerced to 0/1 integer and multiplied by dtag by
      # hand. `acc_a_x_dtag` is then one ordinary numeric predictor: nothing to
      # expand, nothing to alias, no name matching, and its coefficient is
      #   log(OR at dtag=1) - log(OR at dtag=0) = log(OR_alt/OR_ref) = log(ROR).
      dd <- flags %>%
        dplyr::filter(line == L) %>%
        dplyr::transmute(
          Sample = factor(Sample),
          dtag   = as.integer(treatment != ref_treatment),   # 0 = ref, 1 = alt
          acc_a  = as.integer(.data[[paste0("acc_", pr[1])]]),
          acc_b  = as.integer(.data[[paste0("acc_", pr[2])]])) %>%
        dplyr::filter(!is.na(dtag), !is.na(acc_a), !is.na(acc_b)) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(Sample       = droplevels(Sample),
                      acc_a_x_dtag = acc_a * dtag)

      # Counted AFTER filtering, so they describe the fibers the model saw.
      base <- tibble::tibble(
        line = L, pair = paste(pr[1], pr[2], sep = " – "),
        peak1 = pr[1], peak2 = pr[2],
        n_fibers_total = nrow(dd),
        n_fibers_ref   = sum(dd$dtag == 0L),
        n_fibers_alt   = sum(dd$dtag == 1L))

      if (nrow(dd) == 0 || dplyr::n_distinct(dd$dtag) < 2) {
        return(dplyr::bind_cols(base, tibble::tibble(
          ror = NA_real_, ror_ci_lo = NA_real_, ror_ci_hi = NA_real_,
          p_interaction = NA_real_,
          glm_note = "only one treatment present -- not comparable")))
      }

      fit <- tryCatch({
        m0 <- stats::glm(acc_b ~ acc_a + Sample,
                         family = stats::binomial, data = dd)
        m1 <- stats::glm(acc_b ~ acc_a + Sample + acc_a_x_dtag,
                         family = stats::binomial, data = dd)

        # Keep this: coef() retains NAs, summary()$coefficients silently drops
        # them, so this is the only place aliasing is visible.
        aliased <- names(stats::coef(m1))[is.na(stats::coef(m1))]
        if (length(aliased) > 0) {
          stop(sprintf("rank-deficient model, aliased coefficient(s): %s",
                       paste(aliased, collapse = ", ")))
        }

        co <- summary(m1)$coefficients
        if (!"acc_a_x_dtag" %in% rownames(co)) {
          stop("interaction term absent from the fit")
        }
        est <- co["acc_a_x_dtag", "Estimate"]
        se  <- co["acc_a_x_dtag", "Std. Error"]
        an  <- stats::anova(m0, m1, test = "LRT")

        list(ror = exp(est),
             lo  = exp(est - stats::qnorm(0.975) * se),
             hi  = exp(est + stats::qnorm(0.975) * se),
             p   = an$`Pr(>Chi)`[2],
             note = sprintf(paste0("logistic interaction (explicit acc_a x dtag ",
                                   "column), LRT 1 df; ROR = OR_%s / OR_%s"),
                            alt_treatment, ref_treatment))
      }, error = function(e) list(ror = NA_real_, lo = NA_real_, hi = NA_real_,
                                  p = NA_real_,
                                  note = paste("failed:", conditionMessage(e))))

      dplyr::bind_cols(base, tibble::tibble(
        ror = fit$ror, ror_ci_lo = fit$lo, ror_ci_hi = fit$hi,
        p_interaction = fit$p, glm_note = fit$note))
    })
  })

  out %>% dplyr::mutate(
    p_interaction_adj = stats::p.adjust(p_interaction, method = p_adjust_method))
}

# (2) CROSS-CHECK: Wald test on the two pooled MH log ORs.
# group_meta: tibble(group, line, treatment)
compare_or_treatments_wald <- function(pooled_df, group_meta,
                                       ref_treatment = "DMSO",
                                       p_adjust_method = "BH") {
  pooled_df %>%
    dplyr::left_join(group_meta, by = "group") %>%
    dplyr::group_by(line, pair) %>%
    dplyr::group_modify(function(dd, k) {
      # Every branch returns the SAME columns, so a failure in one line x pair
      # cannot make a column disappear from the bound result (which would then
      # break the figure annotation and the export downstream).
      blank <- tibble::tibble(
        group_ref = NA_character_, group_alt = NA_character_,
        or_ref = NA_real_, or_alt = NA_real_,
        ror_wald = NA_real_, ror_wald_ci_lo = NA_real_, ror_wald_ci_hi = NA_real_,
        p_wald = NA_real_, wald_note = NA_character_)

      ref <- dd %>% dplyr::filter(treatment == ref_treatment)
      alt <- dd %>% dplyr::filter(treatment != ref_treatment)
      if (nrow(ref) != 1 || nrow(alt) != 1) {
        blank$wald_note <- "need exactly one group per treatment"
        return(blank)
      }
      blank$group_ref <- ref$group; blank$group_alt <- alt$group
      blank$or_ref    <- ref$mh_or; blank$or_alt    <- alt$mh_or

      dlog <- log(alt$mh_or) - log(ref$mh_or)
      se   <- sqrt(alt$se_log_or^2 + ref$se_log_or^2)
      blank$ror_wald <- exp(dlog)
      if (!is.finite(dlog) || !is.finite(se) || se == 0) {
        blank$wald_note <- "SE undefined (empty cell) -- use the interaction test"
        return(blank)
      }
      blank$ror_wald_ci_lo <- exp(dlog - stats::qnorm(0.975) * se)
      blank$ror_wald_ci_hi <- exp(dlog + stats::qnorm(0.975) * se)
      blank$p_wald         <- 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(dlog / se))
      blank$wald_note      <- "Wald on difference of pooled MH log ORs"
      blank
    }) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(p_wald_adj = stats::p.adjust(p_wald, method = p_adjust_method))
}
```

# 5. Plot functions

## 5a. Triangle plot (LD-style)

```{r plot-triangle}
# Summits sit evenly spaced on a baseline; each pair's diamond is centred above
# the midpoint of its two summits at a height proportional to their separation,
# so adjacent pairs sit low and distal pairs form the apex.
#
#   FILL  = mean codependency (obs - exp) across replicates
#   LABEL = the individual replicate values that mean is made of
#
# `limits` should be supplied when several panels are combined, so all panels
# share one colour scale. Works for any number of summits and replicates; with
# exactly two summits the plot is a single diamond.
# show_numbers = FALSE gives the colour-only version used in the main figure
# (the per-replicate numbers then live in the metrics workbook).
plot_codep_triangle_reps <- function(perrep_df, summits,
                                     title = "", subtitle = NULL,
                                     limits = NULL,
                                     show_numbers = TRUE,
                                     rep_label_fn = function(x) {
                                       lab <- stringr::str_extract(x, "rep[0-9]+")
                                       ifelse(is.na(lab), x, lab)
                                     },
                                     digits = 1,
                                     mark_sig = TRUE, sig_col = "p_adj",
                                     sig_cut = 0.05) {
  peaks  <- names(summits)
  pos    <- setNames(seq_along(peaks) - 1, peaks)   # 0, 1, 2, ...
  combos <- utils::combn(peaks, 2, simplify = FALSE)

  df <- perrep_df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(rep_lab = rep_label_fn(Sample)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(rep_lab)

  # pull a pair's rows regardless of peak1 / peak2 order
  get_rows <- function(a, b) {
    df %>% dplyr::filter((peak1 == a & peak2 == b) | (peak1 == b & peak2 == a))
  }

  fmt <- function(v) sprintf(paste0("%+.", digits, "f"), v * 100)

  cell <- purrr::map_dfr(combos, function(pr) {
    rows <- get_rows(pr[1], pr[2])
    if (nrow(rows) == 0) {
      return(tibble::tibble(pair = paste(pr[1], pr[2], sep = " – "),
                            i = pos[[pr[1]]], j = pos[[pr[2]]],
                            mean_codep = NA_real_, label = "n/a"))
    }
    star <- if (mark_sig && sig_col %in% names(rows)) {
      ifelse(!is.na(rows[[sig_col]]) & rows[[sig_col]] < sig_cut, "*", "")
    } else rep("", nrow(rows))
    tibble::tibble(
      pair = paste(pr[1], pr[2], sep = " – "),
      i = pos[[pr[1]]], j = pos[[pr[2]]],
      mean_codep = mean(rows$codependency, na.rm = TRUE),
      label = paste(sprintf("%s %s%s", rows$rep_lab, fmt(rows$codependency), star),
                    collapse = "\n")
    )
  })

  # unit rhombi (N/E/S/W vertices offset by 0.5) so neighbouring diamonds tile
  diamonds <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
    list(cell$pair, cell$i, cell$j, cell$mean_codep),
    function(pr, i, j, mc) {
      cx <- (i + j) / 2; cy <- (j - i) / 2
      tibble::tibble(pair = pr, mean_codep = mc,
                     x = c(cx, cx + 0.5, cx, cx - 0.5),
                     y = c(cy + 0.5, cy, cy - 0.5, cy))
    })

  labels   <- cell %>% dplyr::mutate(x = (i + j) / 2, y = (j - i) / 2)
  baseline <- tibble::tibble(peak = peaks, x = unname(pos), y = 0)

  if (is.null(limits)) {
    lim <- suppressWarnings(max(abs(cell$mean_codep), na.rm = TRUE))
    if (!is.finite(lim) || lim == 0) lim <- 0.01   # guard: all-NA or all-zero
    limits <- c(-lim, lim)
  }

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_polygon(data = diamonds,
                 aes(x = x, y = y, group = pair, fill = mean_codep),
                 colour = "black", linewidth = 0.25)

  if (show_numbers) {
    p <- p + geom_text(data = labels, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
                       size = 3, lineheight = 1.05)
  }

  p +
    geom_point(data = baseline, aes(x = x, y = y), size = 2) +
    geom_text(data = baseline, aes(x = x, y = y, label = peak),
              vjust = 2.2, fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "steelblue", mid = "white", high = "firebrick",
                         midpoint = 0, limits = limits, oob = scales::squish,
                         na.value = "grey90",
                         name = "mean codependency\n(obs − exp)",
                         labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
    coord_fixed(clip = "off") +
    theme_void(base_size = 13) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme(plot.title    = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold",
                                       margin = margin(b = 4)),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 9, colour = "grey30",
                                       margin = margin(b = 8)),
          plot.margin   = margin(10, 10, 25, 10))
}

# One triangle per group on a SHARED colour scale, then arranged.
# group_levels fixes the panel order (e.g. SNAI DMSO, SNAI dTag, TWIST DMSO...).
triangle_panels_by_group <- function(perrep_df, summits, group_levels = NULL,
                                     ncol = 2, ...) {
  groups <- group_levels %||% sort(unique(perrep_df$group))
  groups <- groups[groups %in% unique(perrep_df$group)]

  means <- perrep_df %>%
    dplyr::group_by(group, pair) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(m = mean(codependency), .groups = "drop")
  lim <- suppressWarnings(max(abs(means$m), na.rm = TRUE))
  if (!is.finite(lim) || lim == 0) lim <- 0.01

  plots <- purrr::map(groups, function(g) {
    plot_codep_triangle_reps(
      perrep_df %>% dplyr::filter(group == g),
      summits, title = g, limits = c(-lim, lim), ...)
  })
  list(plots = plots, limits = c(-lim, lim),
       arranged = ggpubr::ggarrange(plotlist = plots, ncol = ncol,
                                    nrow = ceiling(length(plots) / ncol),
                                    common.legend = TRUE, legend = "right"))
}
```

## 5b. Odds ratio forest plot

```{r plot-forest}
# ggplot2 >= 3.5 renamed `trans` to `transform`; support both.
.scale_x_log2 <- function(...) {
  if (utils::packageVersion("ggplot2") >= "3.5.0") {
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(transform = "log2", ...)
  } else {
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(trans = "log2", ...)
  }
}

# Group-comparable forest plot.
#   one facet per summit pair; groups stacked on the y axis in a fixed order,
#   so DMSO and dTag for the same TF sit next to each other
#   large diamond + CI = Mantel-Haenszel pooled OR for that group
#   small open points  = individual replicates (Fisher)
# Fisher ORs are Inf / 0 whenever a cell is empty; those are squished to
# `clamp` and drawn with an open symbol so they are not read as finite.
# or_compare : optional output of the DMSO-vs-dTag comparison, i.e. columns
#              pair, line, group_ref, group_alt, ror, p_interaction_adj. Drawn
#              as a bracket spanning the two rows of each cell line.
plot_codep_forest_groups <- function(pooled_df, perrep_df = NULL,
                                     group_levels = NULL,
                                     group_colours = NULL,
                                     clamp = NULL,
                                     point_size = 2.6,
                                     or_compare = NULL,
                                     title = "Association between summits (odds ratio)",
                                     subtitle = NULL) {
  glev <- group_levels %||% sort(unique(pooled_df$group))

  pooled <- pooled_df %>%
    dplyr::transmute(pair, group, or = mh_or, lo = mh_ci_lo, hi = mh_ci_hi,
                     p = p_mh_adj, kind = "pooled")

  df <- pooled
  if (!is.null(perrep_df)) {
    df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
      df,
      perrep_df %>%
        dplyr::transmute(pair, group, or = odds_ratio, lo = or_ci_lo,
                         hi = or_ci_hi, p = p_adj, kind = "replicate"))
  }

  # Axis limits, data-driven by default. THIS MATTERS: with tens of thousands
  # of fibers per replicate, SE(log OR) is ~0.02 and the 95% CI is only a few
  # percent wide. On a hard-coded wide axis such as c(0.05, 20) that interval
  # is narrower than the plotting symbol, so the error bars are invisible even
  # though they were computed correctly. Fitting the axis to the data (and
  # shrinking the point) is what makes them visible.
  if (is.null(clamp)) {
    fin <- c(df$or, df$lo, df$hi)
    fin <- fin[is.finite(fin) & fin > 0]
    if (length(fin) == 0) fin <- c(0.5, 2)
    clamp <- c(min(fin, 1) / 1.15, max(fin, 1) * 1.15)
  }

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      group    = factor(group, levels = glev),
      censored = !is.finite(or) | or <= clamp[1] | or >= clamp[2],
      dplyr::across(c(or, lo, hi), ~ pmin(pmax(.x, clamp[1]), clamp[2])),
      sig      = ifelse(!is.na(p) & p < 0.05, "p < 0.05", "n.s."),
      kind     = factor(kind, levels = c("pooled", "replicate"))) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(group))

  pool_only <- df %>% dplyr::filter(kind == "pooled")
  rep_only  <- df %>% dplyr::filter(kind == "replicate")

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = or, y = group)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4,
               colour = "grey40")

  if (nrow(rep_only) > 0) {
    p <- p + geom_point(data = rep_only, aes(colour = group),
                        shape = 1, size = point_size * 0.6, alpha = 0.85,
                        position = position_nudge(y = 0.18))
  }

  p <- p +
    # End caps on, so a very narrow CI still reads as an interval rather than
    # disappearing under the marker.
    geom_errorbarh(data = pool_only, aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi, colour = group),
                   height = 0.16, linewidth = 0.55) +
    geom_point(data = pool_only, aes(colour = group, shape = censored),
               size = point_size) +
    geom_text(data = pool_only,
              aes(label = ifelse(is.na(p), "",
                          ifelse(p < 0.001, "***",
                          ifelse(p < 0.01, "**",
                          ifelse(p < 0.05, "*", ""))))),
              nudge_y = -0.24, size = 4, colour = "grey20")

  # DMSO vs dTag brackets, one per cell line per facet.
  if (!is.null(or_compare) && nrow(or_compare) > 0) {
    ann <- or_compare %>%
      dplyr::filter(pair %in% unique(df$pair),
                    group_ref %in% glev, group_alt %in% glev) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        y1   = match(group_ref, rev(glev)),   # matches scale_y_discrete below
        y2   = match(group_alt, rev(glev)),
        ymid = (y1 + y2) / 2,
        xb   = clamp[2] / 1.25,
        label = ifelse(is.na(ror), "ROR n/a",
                       sprintf("ROR %.2f, p=%s", ror,
                               format.pval(p_interaction_adj, digits = 2, eps = 1e-4))))
    p <- p +
      geom_segment(data = ann, aes(x = xb, xend = xb, y = y1, yend = y2),
                   inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey45") +
      geom_text(data = ann, aes(x = clamp[2], y = ymid, label = label),
                inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 2.7,
                colour = "grey20")
  }

  p +
    facet_wrap(~ pair, ncol = 1) +
    .scale_x_log2(labels = function(x) signif(x, 2)) +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(glev)) +
    # Only advertise clamping when something is actually clamped, and say what
    # it means: the point sits ON the axis limit, its true value is beyond it.
    scale_shape_manual(
      values = c(`FALSE` = 18, `TRUE` = 5),
      labels = c(`FALSE` = "OR and 95% CI within axis limits",
                 `TRUE`  = "clamped: true OR or CI beyond axis limits"),
      name = NULL, drop = FALSE,
      guide = if (any(pool_only$censored, na.rm = TRUE)) "legend" else "none") +
    { if (is.null(group_colours)) scale_colour_discrete(guide = "none")
      else scale_colour_manual(values = group_colours, guide = "none") } +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle,
         x = "Odds ratio for co-accessibility (log2 scale) (1 = independent)",
         y = NULL) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", colour = NA),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"),
          legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

## 5c. Supplementary plots

```{r plot-supp}
# One point per replicate, crossbar at the group mean, hline at 0.
# Significance is counted per group x pair (counting per pair only would
# mislabel panels once faceted by group).
plot_codep_perrep <- function(perrep_df, facet_group = TRUE,
                              show_sig = TRUE, sig_col = "p_adj",
                              group_levels = NULL,
                              title = "Peak co-dependency by replicate",
                              subtitle = NULL) {
  has_grp <- !all(is.na(perrep_df$group))
  if (has_grp && !is.null(group_levels)) {
    perrep_df <- perrep_df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(group = factor(group, levels = group_levels))
  }
  keys <- if (has_grp && facet_group) c("group", "pair") else "pair"

  mn <- perrep_df %>%
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(keys))) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(m = mean(codependency), .groups = "drop")

  p <- ggplot(perrep_df, aes(x = pair, y = codependency)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4, colour = "grey20") +
    geom_crossbar(data = mn, aes(x = pair, y = m, ymin = m, ymax = m),
                  width = 0.55, linewidth = 0.4, fatten = 0, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = Sample,
                   shape = factor(low_fibers, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE))),
               position = position_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0), size = 2.6) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 1),
                       labels = c(`FALSE` = "ok", `TRUE` = "low n"),
                       name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle,
         x = NULL, y = "codependency (obs − exp)", colour = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(legend.position = "right",
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))

  if (show_sig && sig_col %in% names(perrep_df)) {
    span <- diff(range(perrep_df$codependency, na.rm = TRUE))
    if (!is.finite(span) || span == 0) span <- 0.02
    stars <- perrep_df %>%
      dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(keys))) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(y   = max(codependency, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.06 * span,
                       lab = paste0(sum(.data[[sig_col]] < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
                                    "/", dplyr::n(), " reps *"),
                       .groups = "drop")
    p <- p + geom_text(data = stars, aes(x = pair, y = y, label = lab),
                       inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3, vjust = 0)
  }
  if (has_grp && facet_group) p <- p + facet_wrap(~ group)
  p
}

plot_codep_obsexp_perrep <- function(perrep_df,
                                     title = "Observed vs expected co-accessibility",
                                     subtitle = NULL) {
  df <- perrep_df %>%
    dplyr::select(Sample, group, pair,
                  observed = observed_coaccessibility,
                  expected = expected_coaccessibility, p_adj) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(c(observed, expected),
                        names_to = "type", values_to = "fraction")

  ggplot(df, aes(x = Sample, y = fraction, fill = type)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +
    facet_wrap(~ pair) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(observed = "firebrick", expected = "grey65")) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, x = NULL,
         y = "Fraction of fibers", fill = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(legend.position = "top",
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))
}
```
