# 6. RUN — one pass per enhancer

```{r run-fn}
# Everything one enhancer needs, in the order the sections above define it.
# Returns a list; nothing is written to disk here (see sections 7-9).
run_enhancer <- function(label, cfg, d) {
  message("\n==== ", label, " (", cfg$chrom, ", ",
          length(cfg$summits), " summits, ", length(cfg$groups), " groups) ====")

  # Re-seeded per enhancer so each enhancer's bootstrap CIs are reproducible
  # on their own and do not depend on how many enhancers ran before it.
  set.seed(BOOT_SEED)

  sample_groups <- SAMPLE_GROUPS[cfg$groups]           # keeps the config order
  samples       <- unlist(sample_groups, use.names = FALSE)
  group_meta    <- GROUP_META %>% dplyr::filter(group %in% cfg$groups)
  sample_meta   <- tibble::tibble(
    Sample = samples,
    group  = rep(names(sample_groups), lengths(sample_groups))
  ) %>% dplyr::left_join(group_meta, by = "group")
  stopifnot(!any(is.na(sample_meta$line)))

  codep <- compute_codependency_perrep(
    d$reads, d$msps, cfg$summits,
    chrom_sel       = cfg$chrom,
    min_width       = MIN_WIDTH,
    fiber_set       = FIBER_SET,
    samples         = samples,
    sample_groups   = sample_groups,
    min_fibers      = MIN_FIBERS,
    boot            = N_BOOT,
    p_adjust_method = P_ADJUST_METHOD,
    p_adjust_scope  = P_ADJUST_SCOPE)

  rep_summary <- summarise_codependency_reps(codep, by_group = TRUE)
  pooled      <- pool_codependency_mh(codep, by_group = TRUE,
                                      p_adjust_method = P_ADJUST_METHOD)

  # Marginal accessibility per summit per sample. NB: computed on all fibers
  # spanning each summit, a larger set than the co-dependency population.
  marginals <- compute_summit_accessibility(
    d$reads, d$msps, cfg$summits,
    chrom_sel = cfg$chrom, min_width = MIN_WIDTH,
    samples = samples, by_sample = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(sample_meta %>% dplyr::select(Sample, group), by = "Sample") %>%
    dplyr::relocate(group, .after = Sample)

  # ---- DMSO vs dTag ---------------------------------------------------------
  or_cmp_glm <- compare_or_treatments_glm(
    d$reads, d$msps, cfg$summits, sample_meta,
    chrom_sel       = cfg$chrom,
    min_width       = MIN_WIDTH,
    fiber_set       = FIBER_SET,
    ref_treatment   = REF_TREATMENT,
    p_adjust_method = P_ADJUST_METHOD)

  or_cmp_wald <- compare_or_treatments_wald(
    pooled, group_meta, ref_treatment = REF_TREATMENT,
    p_adjust_method = P_ADJUST_METHOD)

  # Which two groups each cell line contrasts. Derived from group_meta rather
  # than borrowed from compare_or_treatments_wald(), which returns NA group
  # labels on its bail-out branch -- that would silently skip the tetrachoric
  # check below even when the GLM result is perfectly valid.
  contrast_groups <- group_meta %>%
    dplyr::group_by(line) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      group_ref = group[treatment == REF_TREATMENT][1],
      group_alt = group[treatment != REF_TREATMENT][1],
      .groups = "drop")

  or_compare <- or_cmp_glm %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      # wald_note is carried through so section 8 can verify it, and dropped
      # from the exported sheet there.
      or_cmp_wald %>% dplyr::select(line, pair, ror_wald,
                                    ror_wald_ci_lo, ror_wald_ci_hi,
                                    p_wald, p_wald_adj, wald_note),
      by = c("line", "pair")) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(contrast_groups, by = "line") %>%
    dplyr::relocate(group_ref, group_alt, .after = pair) %>%
    # Pooled MH odds ratio for each contrasted group, taken straight from
    # `pooled` (one row per group x pair, so no fan-out).
    dplyr::left_join(pooled %>% dplyr::select(group, pair, or_ref = mh_or),
                     by = c("group_ref" = "group", "pair")) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(pooled %>% dplyr::select(group, pair, or_alt = mh_or),
                     by = c("group_alt" = "group", "pair")) %>%
    # Tetrachoric sensitivity check: the replicate-mean, threshold-invariant
    # correlation for each contrasted group. If rho moves the same way as the
    # odds ratio, the change in association is not an artifact of the treatment
    # shifting marginal accessibility. Comparisons in which neither measure
    # moves appreciably are recorded as NA -- they carry no directional
    # information and must not be scored as contradictions.
    dplyr::left_join(rep_summary %>% dplyr::select(group, pair, rho_ref = mean_rho),
                     by = c("group_ref" = "group", "pair")) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(rep_summary %>% dplyr::select(group, pair, rho_alt = mean_rho),
                     by = c("group_alt" = "group", "pair")) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      delta_rho = rho_alt - rho_ref,
      rho_direction_agrees = dplyr::case_when(
        is.na(delta_rho) | is.na(ror) | !is.finite(ror)     ~ NA,
        abs(delta_rho) < RHO_TOL | abs(log(ror)) < log(OR_TOL) ~ NA,
        TRUE ~ sign(delta_rho) == sign(log(ror))))

  # ---- diagnostics ----------------------------------------------------------
  # An empty 2x2 cell means the common odds ratio is 0 or Inf and the variance
  # of its log does not exist; the CI then comes from the Haldane fallback.
  if (any(pooled$any_zero_cell)) {
    message(label, ": pairs with an empty 2x2 cell (CI uses Haldane correction):")
    print(pooled %>% dplyr::filter(any_zero_cell) %>%
            dplyr::select(group, pair, mh_or, mh_ci_lo, mh_ci_hi,
                          min_cell, ci_method))
  }

  # The Wald ROR is or_alt/or_ref straight from the pooled MH tables, so it
  # fixes the orientation. If the GLM ROR is its reciprocal, the interaction
  # term is being read the wrong way round (see compare_or_treatments_glm).
  chk <- or_compare %>%
    dplyr::filter(is.finite(ror), is.finite(ror_wald)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(dlog = log(ror) - log(ror_wald))
  if (nrow(chk) > 0 && max(abs(chk$dlog)) > 0.15) {
    stop(label, ": GLM and Wald RORs disagree in direction or magnitude:\n",
         paste(sprintf("  %s / %s: ror=%.3f ror_wald=%.3f",
                       chk$line, chk$pair, chk$ror, chk$ror_wald), collapse = "\n"))
  }

  list(label         = label,
       config        = cfg,
       samples       = samples,
       sample_groups = sample_groups,
       group_levels  = names(sample_groups),
       group_colours = GROUP_COLOURS[names(sample_groups)],
       codep         = codep,
       rep_summary   = rep_summary,
       pooled        = pooled,
       marginals     = marginals,
       or_compare    = or_compare)
}
```

```{r run-all}
res <- purrr::imap(ENHANCERS, function(cfg, label) run_enhancer(label, cfg, d))
```

# 7. Main figures

Two PDFs per enhancer:

* `<label>_codep_oddsratio_groups_min<w>.pdf` — pooled Mantel-Haenszel odds
  ratio per group, one facet per summit pair, replicate ORs as open points,
  DMSO-vs-dTag ROR bracket.
* `<label>_codep_triangles_colouronly_min<w>.pdf` — LD-style triangle per
  group on a shared colour scale, fill = mean codependency (obs − exp).

```{r fig-forest, fig.width=8, fig.height=7}
forest_plots <- purrr::imap(res, function(r, label) {
  p <- plot_codep_forest_groups(
    r$pooled, r$codep,
    group_levels  = r$group_levels,
    group_colours = r$group_colours,
    or_compare    = r$or_compare,
    title = sprintf("Association between summits (odds ratio) - %s", label))

  # Width follows the number of stacked groups (4 groups -> 7 in, 2 -> 5 in),
  # height follows the number of facets (one per summit pair).
  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, sprintf("%s_codep_oddsratio_groups_min%s.pdf",
                                    label, MIN_WIDTH)),
         plot   = p,
         width  = 3 + length(r$group_levels),
         height = 0.5 + 2 * length(unique(r$codep$pair)),
         device = PDF_DEV)
  p
})
purrr::walk(forest_plots, print)
```

```{r fig-triangles, fig.width=11, fig.height=9}
# Colour only: the per-replicate numbers live in the metrics workbook, and the
# fill is described in the figure legend text rather than a subtitle.
#
# NB: pass `plot =` to ggsave() explicitly. Without it ggsave() falls back to
# last_plot(), which for a ggarrange object is the last individual panel built,
# not the arranged figure -- that is why a saved PDF can differ from the
# on-screen one.
triangle_plots <- purrr::imap(res, function(r, label) {
  tri <- triangle_panels_by_group(
    r$codep, r$config$summits,
    group_levels = r$group_levels, ncol = 2,
    show_numbers = FALSE)

  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, sprintf("%s_codep_triangles_colouronly_min%s.pdf",
                                    label, MIN_WIDTH)),
         plot = tri$arranged, width = 6, height = 6, device = PDF_DEV)
  tri$arranged
})
purrr::walk(triangle_plots, print)
```

# 8. Combined summary workbook

One workbook covering both enhancers. Every sheet carries an `enhancer`
column. Redundancies present in the two original per-enhancer workbooks have
been removed:

* `replicate_summary` — folded into `summary` (mean / sd / sign of the
  per-replicate codependency now sit beside the pooled OR for the same
  group × pair).
* `fiber_depth` — exactly equal to `n_fibers` in `per_replicate`, because
  `MIN_WIDTH` filters MSPs and never fibers, so the analysis population is the
  same count. Dropped.
* Constant note columns (`mh_note`, `glm_note`, `wald_note`, `fiber_set`) —
  moved to `config` / `README`, and checked programmatically below so a
  non-standard value cannot pass unnoticed.
* `min_codep` / `max_codep`, `peak1` / `peak2`, `any_zero_cell`,
  `n_fibers_total` — recoverable from columns that are kept.

```{r combine-tables}
.tag <- function(x, label) dplyr::mutate(x, enhancer = label, .before = 1)

# ---- constant columns are dropped from the sheets, so verify they really are
# constant. Anything unexpected must surface here rather than vanish.
.constant_check <- function(values, expected, what) {
  bad <- setdiff(unique(as.character(values)), expected)
  if (length(bad) > 0) {
    warning(sprintf("%s is not the expected constant -- found: %s",
                    what, paste(bad, collapse = " | ")))
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}
.constant_check(unlist(lapply(res, function(r) r$codep$fiber_set)),
                FIBER_SET, "fiber_set")
.constant_check(unlist(lapply(res, function(r) r$pooled$mh_note)),
                "asymptotic CMH p", "mh_note")

# ---- 8a. headline summary: one row per enhancer x group x summit pair -------
summary_tbl <- purrr::imap_dfr(res, function(r, label) {
  r$pooled %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      r$rep_summary %>%
        dplyr::select(group, pair, mean_obs, mean_exp, mean_codep, sd_codep,
                      same_sign, any_low_n, mean_rho, min_rho, max_rho),
      by = c("group", "pair")) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(group = factor(group, levels = r$group_levels)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(group, pair) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(group = as.character(group)) %>%
    .tag(label)
}) %>%
  dplyr::select(enhancer, group, pair, n_reps, total_fibers,
                mean_obs, mean_exp, mean_codep, sd_codep, same_sign, any_low_n,
                mh_or, mh_ci_lo, mh_ci_hi, p_mh, p_mh_adj,
                mean_rho, min_rho, max_rho, woolf_p, min_cell, ci_method)

# ---- 8b. per-replicate detail (the 2x2 tables everything else derives from) --
perrep_tbl <- purrr::imap_dfr(res, function(r, label) {
  r$codep %>%
    dplyr::mutate(group = factor(group, levels = r$group_levels)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(group, pair, Sample) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(group = as.character(group)) %>%
    .tag(label)
}) %>%
  dplyr::select(enhancer, Sample, group, pair, n_fibers,
                n11, n10, n01, n00, frac_peak1, frac_peak2,
                observed_coaccessibility, expected_coaccessibility,
                codependency, boot_ci_lo, boot_ci_hi,
                odds_ratio, or_ci_lo, or_ci_hi, rho_tetrachoric,
                p_fisher, p_adj, low_fibers)

# ---- 8c. DMSO vs dTag --------------------------------------------------------
or_tbl_full <- purrr::imap_dfr(res, function(r, label) .tag(r$or_compare, label))

# The note columns are dropped from the sheet, so anything non-standard has to
# surface here instead of disappearing silently.
odd_notes <- or_tbl_full %>%
  dplyr::filter(!grepl("^logistic interaction", glm_note) |
                !grepl("^Wald on difference",  wald_note))
if (nrow(odd_notes) > 0) {
  warning("Non-standard DMSO-vs-dTag fits (inspect before reporting):")
  print(odd_notes %>% dplyr::select(enhancer, line, pair, glm_note, wald_note))
}

or_tbl <- or_tbl_full %>%
  dplyr::arrange(enhancer, line, pair) %>%
  dplyr::select(enhancer, line, pair, group_ref, group_alt,
                n_fibers_ref, n_fibers_alt, or_ref, or_alt,
                ror, ror_ci_lo, ror_ci_hi, p_interaction, p_interaction_adj,
                ror_wald, ror_wald_ci_lo, ror_wald_ci_hi, p_wald_adj,
                rho_ref, rho_alt, delta_rho, rho_direction_agrees)

# The sensitivity analysis is only informative if it is actually checked, and
# NA rows must be counted as "not checked", never folded into the pass count.
n_pass   <- sum(or_tbl$rho_direction_agrees %in% TRUE)
n_fail   <- sum(or_tbl$rho_direction_agrees %in% FALSE)
n_notest <- sum(is.na(or_tbl$rho_direction_agrees))

if (n_fail > 0) {
  warning("Tetrachoric correlation and odds ratio move in OPPOSITE directions ",
          "for the comparisons below. The change in odds ratio may reflect the ",
          "shift in marginal accessibility rather than a change in association ",
          "-- do not report these as changes in coupling without addressing it.")
  print(or_tbl %>%
          dplyr::filter(rho_direction_agrees %in% FALSE) %>%
          dplyr::select(enhancer, line, pair, or_ref, or_alt, ror,
                        rho_ref, rho_alt, delta_rho))
}
if (n_notest > 0) {
  message(n_notest, " comparison(s) were NOT testable (rho undefined, or ",
          "neither measure moved by more than RHO_TOL = ", RHO_TOL,
          " / OR_TOL = ", OR_TOL, "):")
  print(or_tbl %>%
          dplyr::filter(is.na(rho_direction_agrees)) %>%
          dplyr::select(enhancer, line, pair, ror, rho_ref, rho_alt, delta_rho))
}
message(sprintf(
  "Tetrachoric sensitivity check: %d agree, %d disagree, %d not testable (of %d).",
  n_pass, n_fail, n_notest, nrow(or_tbl)))

# ---- 8d. marginal accessibility ---------------------------------------------
marginals_tbl <- purrr::imap_dfr(res, function(r, label) .tag(r$marginals, label))

# ---- 8e. config --------------------------------------------------------------
config_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(
    enhancer  = "(global)",
    parameter = c("min_width_main", "fiber_set", "min_fibers", "n_boot",
                  "boot_seed", "p_adjust_method", "p_adjust_scope",
                  "ref_treatment", "mh_p_type", "rho_tol", "or_tol",
                  "date", "R_version", "ggplot2_version"),
    value     = c(as.character(MIN_WIDTH), FIBER_SET,
                  as.character(MIN_FIBERS), as.character(N_BOOT),
                  as.character(BOOT_SEED),
                  P_ADJUST_METHOD, P_ADJUST_SCOPE, REF_TREATMENT,
                  "asymptotic CMH (>=2 replicates per group)",
                  as.character(RHO_TOL), as.character(OR_TOL),
                  as.character(Sys.Date()),
                  paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep = "."),
                  as.character(utils::packageVersion("ggplot2")))),
  purrr::imap_dfr(res, function(r, label) {
    tibble::tibble(
      enhancer  = label,
      parameter = c("chrom", "summits", "n_summit_pairs", "groups",
                    "n_samples", "samples"),
      value     = c(r$config$chrom,
                    paste(sprintf("%s=%d", names(r$config$summits),
                                  r$config$summits), collapse = "; "),
                    as.character(choose(length(r$config$summits), 2)),
                    paste(r$group_levels, collapse = "; "),
                    as.character(length(r$samples)),
                    paste(r$samples, collapse = "; ")))
  })
)

# ---- 8f. README --------------------------------------------------------------
readme <- tibble::tribble(
  ~sheet,          ~column,                       ~meaning,
  "(all)",         "enhancer",                    "which enhancer the row belongs to; the two enhancers are analysed independently and nothing is adjusted or pooled across them",
  "summary",       "group / pair",                "experimental group and summit pair; ONE ROW PER enhancer x group x pair -- this is the headline table",
  "summary",       "n_reps / total_fibers",       "replicates contributing, and fibers summed over them",
  "summary",       "mean_obs / mean_exp",         "replicate mean of observed and expected co-accessibility",
  "summary",       "mean_codep / sd_codep",       "replicate mean and sd of codependency = observed - expected; >0 cooperative, <0 mutually exclusive",
  "summary",       "same_sign",                   "TRUE if all replicates agree in direction",
  "summary",       "any_low_n",                   sprintf("TRUE if any replicate had < %d fibers", MIN_FIBERS),
  "summary",       "mh_or, mh_ci_lo/hi",          "Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio stratified by replicate (fibers NOT pooled), with a Robins-Breslow-Greenland 95% CI",
  "summary",       "p_mh / p_mh_adj",             sprintf("asymptotic CMH p and its %s-adjusted value -- p_mh_adj is the headline p-value", P_ADJUST_METHOD),
  "summary",       "mean_rho / min_rho / max_rho","tetrachoric correlation averaged over replicates, and its range. This is the latent-variable correlation that would produce the observed 2x2 table given its own margins: unlike the odds ratio it is invariant to the marginals under a threshold model, so it shows whether an apparent change in association survives a change in accessibility. Computed per replicate and then averaged, so fibers are never pooled across replicates",
  "summary",       "woolf_p",                     "Woolf homogeneity of the OR across replicates; small = replicates disagree and pooling is questionable (very low power with 2 replicates)",
  "summary",       "min_cell",                    "smallest 2x2 cell across replicates; 0 means the exact MH variance is undefined and the CI used the Haldane fallback",
  "summary",       "ci_method",                   "RBG, or RBG after Haldane-Anscombe +0.5 when a cell was empty (interval then approximate)",
  "per_replicate", "n_fibers",                    "fibers in the analysis population for that replicate (spanning ALL summits of the enhancer). MIN_WIDTH filters MSPs, not fibers, so this is also the raw fiber depth over the summit window",
  "per_replicate", "n11/n10/n01/n00",             "2x2 counts: accessible/inaccessible at summit1 x summit2",
  "per_replicate", "frac_peak1 / frac_peak2",     "marginal accessible fraction at each summit ON THIS FIBER SET (not comparable to the marginals sheet)",
  "per_replicate", "observed_coaccessibility",    "P(accessible at both) = n11 / n_fibers",
  "per_replicate", "expected_coaccessibility",    "frac_peak1 * frac_peak2, i.e. independence",
  "per_replicate", "codependency",                "observed - expected",
  "per_replicate", "boot_ci_lo / boot_ci_hi",     sprintf("percentile bootstrap 95%% CI on codependency (%d draws, fibers resampled and both marginals and joint recomputed each draw)", N_BOOT),
  "per_replicate", "odds_ratio, or_ci_lo/hi",     "Fisher exact conditional OR and 95% CI for that replicate (Inf/0 when a cell is empty)",
  "per_replicate", "rho_tetrachoric",             "tetrachoric correlation of that replicate's 2x2 table; threshold-invariant companion to odds_ratio",
  "per_replicate", "p_fisher / p_adj",            sprintf("Fisher exact two-sided p for independence, and its %s-adjusted value (scope = %s)", P_ADJUST_METHOD, P_ADJUST_SCOPE),
  "per_replicate", "low_fibers",                  sprintf("TRUE if n_fibers < %d", MIN_FIBERS),
  "DMSO_vs_dTag",  "-",                           "within each cell line, IS the odds ratio different between DMSO and dTag? A ratio of odds ratios (interaction) -- not answerable by comparing two separate p-values or overlapping CIs",
  "DMSO_vs_dTag",  "or_ref / or_alt",             "pooled MH odds ratio in DMSO / in dTag",
  "DMSO_vs_dTag",  "ror, ror_ci_lo/hi",           "ROR = OR_dTag / OR_DMSO from the fiber-level logistic interaction (PRIMARY). 1 = association unchanged, <1 = weaker after dTag",
  "DMSO_vs_dTag",  "p_interaction(_adj)",         "likelihood-ratio test (1 df) of the acc_a x dTag interaction in acc_b ~ acc_a + Sample + acc_a_x_dtag, fitted with an explicit product column -- the headline DMSO-vs-dTag p-value",
  "DMSO_vs_dTag",  "ror_wald, p_wald_adj",        "independent cross-check: Wald test on the difference of the two pooled MH log ORs. Should agree with ror / p_interaction; the run stops if |log ror - log ror_wald| > 0.15",
  "DMSO_vs_dTag",  "n_fibers_ref / n_fibers_alt", "fibers contributing from each treatment (replicates combined)",
  "DMSO_vs_dTag",  "rho_ref / rho_alt",           "replicate-mean tetrachoric correlation in DMSO / in dTag (threshold-invariant sensitivity analysis)",
  "DMSO_vs_dTag",  "delta_rho",                   "rho_alt - rho_ref. Reported as a difference only: a ratio of correlations is undefined at rho = 0 and changes sign when the two straddle zero",
  "DMSO_vs_dTag",  "rho_direction_agrees",        sprintf("TRUE if the tetrachoric correlation moves in the same direction as the odds ratio, i.e. the change in association is NOT explained by the treatment shifting marginal accessibility. FALSE triggers a warning and the comparison should not be reported as a change in coupling. NA = not testable: rho undefined, or neither measure moved by more than RHO_TOL = %s / OR_TOL = %s, in which case there is no direction to agree about", RHO_TOL, OR_TOL),
  "marginals",     "fraction_accessible",         "marginal accessibility per summit per sample, using EVERY fiber spanning that summit -- a larger population than the co-dependency tables, so do not compare with frac_peak1/2",
  "config",        "-",                           "parameters used for this run, global and per enhancer"
)
```

## 8g. MSP width sensitivity (optional sheets)

Computed here, *before* the workbook is assembled, so that the workbook can be
written and saved exactly once. Skipped unless `MAKE_SUPPLEMENTARY` is TRUE.

```{r sweep-init}
# Always defined, so the export chunk below can test for content without
# needing exists(). NULL = the sweep did not run.
sweep_perrep <- NULL
sweep_pooled <- NULL
```

```{r width-sweep, eval=MAKE_SUPPLEMENTARY}
# Same analysis at several MSP width thresholds. Bootstrap off (boot = 0) --
# this is a robustness table, not a figure.
sweep_perrep <- purrr::imap_dfr(res, function(r, label) {
  purrr::imap_dfr(WIDTH_SWEEP, function(w, wlab) {
    compute_codependency_perrep(
      d$reads, d$msps, r$config$summits,
      chrom_sel       = r$config$chrom,
      min_width       = if (is.na(w)) NULL else w,
      fiber_set       = FIBER_SET,
      samples         = r$samples,
      sample_groups   = r$sample_groups,
      min_fibers      = MIN_FIBERS,
      boot            = 0,
      p_adjust_method = P_ADJUST_METHOD,
      p_adjust_scope  = P_ADJUST_SCOPE
    ) %>% dplyr::mutate(enhancer = label, width_label = wlab, min_width = w,
                        .before = 1)
  })
})

sweep_pooled <- sweep_perrep %>%
  dplyr::group_split(enhancer, width_label) %>%
  purrr::map_dfr(function(dd) {
    pool_codependency_mh(dd, by_group = TRUE,
                         p_adjust_method = P_ADJUST_METHOD) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(enhancer = dd$enhancer[1], width_label = dd$width_label[1],
                    .before = 1)
  })

sweep_pooled
```

## 8h. Write the workbook

```{r export-xlsx}
# The full sheet list is assembled first and the workbook is created, written
# and saved in ONE pass.
#
# DO NOT go back to calling saveWorkbook() twice on the same workbook object
# (e.g. saving here and then appending extra sheets later). openxlsx does not
# reliably retain the sheet data of already-written sheets across a second
# save of the same object: the result is a file in which every sheet written
# before the first save is EMPTY and only the later ones are populated.
sheets <- list(
  README        = readme,
  config        = config_tbl,
  summary       = summary_tbl,
  per_replicate = perrep_tbl,
  DMSO_vs_dTag  = or_tbl,
  marginals     = marginals_tbl
)

# Optional sweep sheets, included only when they were actually computed.
if (!is.null(sweep_perrep) && nrow(sweep_perrep) > 0) {
  sheets$width_sweep_perrep <- sweep_perrep
}
if (!is.null(sweep_pooled) && nrow(sweep_pooled) > 0) {
  sheets$width_sweep_pooled <- sweep_pooled
}

# Guard: a sheet that is empty or has no columns would be written as a blank
# tab, which is easy to miss when the workbook has eight tabs.
empty <- names(sheets)[vapply(sheets, function(x)
  is.null(x) || nrow(x) == 0 || ncol(x) == 0, logical(1))]
if (length(empty) > 0) {
  stop("These sheets have no data and would be written blank: ",
       paste(empty, collapse = ", "))
}

wb  <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()
hdr <- openxlsx::createStyle(textDecoration = "bold", fgFill = "#EFEFEF",
                             border = "bottom", halign = "left")
for (nm in names(sheets)) {
  openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, nm)
  openxlsx::writeData(wb, nm, as.data.frame(sheets[[nm]]), headerStyle = hdr)
  openxlsx::freezePane(wb, nm, firstActiveRow = 2)
  openxlsx::setColWidths(wb, nm, cols = seq_len(ncol(sheets[[nm]])),
                         widths = "auto")
}

xlsx_path <- file.path(
  TABLE_DIR,
  sprintf("%s_codependency_metrics_min%s.xlsx",
          paste(names(ENHANCERS), collapse = "_"), MIN_WIDTH))
openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb, xlsx_path, overwrite = TRUE)

# Read the file back and confirm every sheet actually contains rows. This is
# the check that would have caught the double-save bug immediately.
check_written <- purrr::map_dfr(names(sheets), function(nm) {
  got <- tryCatch(openxlsx::read.xlsx(xlsx_path, sheet = nm),
                  error = function(e) NULL)
  tibble::tibble(sheet = nm,
                 rows_expected = nrow(sheets[[nm]]),
                 rows_in_file  = if (is.null(got)) NA_integer_ else nrow(got))
})
if (any(is.na(check_written$rows_in_file) |
        check_written$rows_in_file < check_written$rows_expected)) {
  print(check_written)
  stop("Workbook written but some sheets are empty or short -- see above.")
}
message("Wrote ", xlsx_path, " (", length(sheets), " sheets, all verified)")
check_written

summary_tbl
```

```{r report-sentences}
# Ready-to-paste numbers for the results text.
summary_tbl %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    enhancer, group, pair,
    sentence = sprintf(
      "OR = %.2f (95%% CI %.2f-%.2f), %s p = %s, n = %d fibers across %d replicates; mean obs - exp = %+.1f%%",
      mh_or, mh_ci_lo, mh_ci_hi, P_ADJUST_METHOD,
      format.pval(p_mh_adj, digits = 2, eps = 1e-4),
      total_fibers, n_reps, 100 * mean_codep)) %>%
  as.data.frame()

or_tbl %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    enhancer, line, pair,
    sentence = sprintf(
      "OR %.2f (%s) vs %.2f (%s); ROR = %.2f (95%% CI %.2f-%.2f), interaction %s p = %s; tetrachoric rho %.3f -> %.3f",
      or_ref, REF_TREATMENT, or_alt, sub("^.* ", "", group_alt),
      ror, ror_ci_lo, ror_ci_hi, P_ADJUST_METHOD,
      format.pval(p_interaction_adj, digits = 2, eps = 1e-4),
      rho_ref, rho_alt)) %>%
  as.data.frame()
```

numbered triangles, the per-replicate dotplot and the observed-vs-expected
bars. The same flag adds the two width-sensitivity sheets to the workbook in
section 8g; that part runs earlier, because the workbook must be assembled and
saved in a single pass.

```{r fig-supp, eval=MAKE_SUPPLEMENTARY, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
for (label in names(res)) {
  r <- res[[label]]

  # Triangles with each replicate's obs - exp printed in the diamond.

  p_var    <- plot_codep_perrep(r$codep, group_levels = r$group_levels,

  p_obsexp <- plot_codep_obsexp_perrep(r$codep, subtitle = label)
  print(p_var); print(p_obsexp)

  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, sprintf("%s_codep_perrep_min%s.pdf", label, MIN_WIDTH)),
         plot = p_var, width = 11, height = 7, device = PDF_DEV)
  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, sprintf("%s_codep_obsexp_min%s.pdf", label, MIN_WIDTH)),
         plot = p_obsexp, width = 11, height = 7, device = PDF_DEV)
}
```
